title: Should I stay or should I go: Hypoxia thresholds of the three‐spined stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus)
content:
Abstract

We established hypoxia avoidance thresholds of three-spined stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) using a customized choice-flume system. Stickleback is an opportunistic species, increasing in abundance in several aquatic systems. We show that sticklebacks avoid oxygen levels commonly reported in many coastal areas. When prey was available in severe hypoxia (10% O2sat), fish still spent 50.9% of the 30-min feeding period in the hypoxic side, compared with 78.5% in the prey side under normoxia. These findings provide a prey-dependent estimate of hypoxia sensitivity in an abundant northern-temperate coastal fish and highlight the need to test whether laboratory thresholds predict field distributions.
